findings.finding: Insights: f(N)=min lcm(d1,d2,d3) for distinct d_i with sum N. For N≈M (M=3^{2025!}), optimal triple often {1, p, N−1−p} where p is smallest prime divisor of N−1 (≠2 if N−1 even). Then f(N)=N−1−p. Hence f(N)/M≈(M+c−1−p)/M≈1+(c−p)/M. Since p≪M, f(N)/M≈1+tiny. Thus g(c)=⌊2025!·f(N)/M⌋/2025! =1 for all N (floor of 2025!·(1+ε) =2025!+⌊2025!·ε⌋, ε<1/2025! ⇒⌊2025!·ε⌋=0). Sum=6 ⇒p/q=6/1 ⇒p+q≡7 (mod 99991).

Insights: f(n)=min lcm(a,b,c) for distinct a+b+c=n. Use X=n−b−c must be multiple of lcm(b,c). For n≈M=3^{2025!}, choose b,c powers of 3 so lcm|M. Then X=M (or small multiple). Compute g(c)=⌊2025!·X/M⌋/2025!≈X/M. For given c’s, X=M when c is sum of two distinct 3‑powers; otherwise X=⌈n/2⌉. Sum g’s → p/q; find p+q mod 99991. Pitfall: ensure distinctness and divisibility; avoid assuming X=M always.

Insights: f(N)=N·min_{S|N} r_min(S) where r_min(S)=min_{x+y+z=S} lcm(x,y,z)/S. Global min r=6/11 from (2,3,6) ⇒ S=11t. So r(N)=6/11 iff 11|N; else need S a divisor of N giving next‑best ratio. For N=M=3^K (no 11), only S=3^s possible → compute r_min(3^s). For N=5M, divisors 3^a·5^b; find best S among those (no 11). For N=M+c, check 11∤N (c≡10 mod11 needed). Compute each g(c)=⌊2025!·f(N)/M⌋/2025!≈f(N)/M. Sum → p/q → output (p+q) mod 99991. Pitfalls: ensure S|N, scaling integer, distinctness, avoid assuming primes of N restrict x_i.

Insights: f(S)=min lcm(a,b,c)=T·(s−1)/s where T=S−1 and s=smallest divisor ≥3 of T. For M=3^{2025!}, T=M+c−1. Since M≡1 (mod p) for any p≤2026, s is the smallest odd divisor of c (if ≤2026) else the smallest odd divisor of T>2026.  

Cases:  
c=0 → T=M−1≡0 (mod 4), s=4.  
c=4M → T=5M−1≡0 (mod 4), s=4.  
c=1848374 (odd part = 924187) → smallest odd prime = 11, s=11.  
c=10162574 (odd part = 5081287, prime; p−1|2025! ⇒ M≡1 (mod p)) → s=5081287.  
c=265710644 (c≡0 (mod 4)) → s=4.  
c=44636594 (odd part = 22318297) → smallest odd prime = 17, s=17.  

For each c>0, floor(2025!·f/M)=2025!·(s−1)/s (integer). For c=0, floor=2025!·3/4−1.  

Thus g(c)= (1/2025!)*floor = (s−1)/s for c>0, and g(0)=3/4−1/2025!.  

Compute sum:  
g(0)=3/4−1/2025!  
g(4M)=15/4−1/2025! (since s=4, (s−1)/s=3/4, but factor 5 from S gives 5·3/4=15/4)  
g(1848374)=(11−1)/11=10/11  
g(10162574)=(5081287−1)/5081287=5081286/5081287

= (33/4) + (10/11+16/17+5081286/5081287) − 3/2025!  

Convert to common denominator → p/q (coprime).

Insights: f(n) = min N = n·(kl/(k+l+kl)) with N = lcm(N/k,N/l) ⇒ ratio r = Nnum/L where L = (k+l+kl)/gcd(kl,k+l+kl). Minimal r’s: 2/3 (L=3), 3/5 (L=5), 4/7 (L=7), 6/11 (L=11)… For n = M+ c, M=3^E, M≡1 (mod L) if 3∤L, else M≡0 (mod 3^a) and ≡1 (mod m). Compute M mod L via CRT. n divisible by L ⇔ (M_mod_L·factor + c)≡0. For given c’s: M (c=0) ⇒ L=3 → r=2/3; 5M (c=4M) ⇒ L=5 → r=3/5; all other M+c (c≡2 mod 3) ⇒ L=5 → r=3/5. Thus g’s: 2/3, 3/5, 2/3, 3/5,3/5,3/5. Sum = 2/3+3/5+2/3+3/5+3/5+3/5 = (4·2/3)+(4·3/5)=8/3+12/5=40/15+36/15=76/15 → p+q=76+15=91. 91 mod 99991 = 91.

Insights: f(n)=min lcm(a,b,c) with a+b+c=n ⇒ f(n)=n·min [lcm(x,y,z)/(x+y+z)] over distinct x,y,z where (x+y+z)|n. Primitive triples give ratios: (2,3,6) →6/11, (1,t,2t) →2t/(1+3t), (a,b,ab) →ab/(a+b+ab). For n=M+ c, M≡1 (mod s) if 3∤s, else compute via CRT (M=3^K). Check divisibility of n by base sums in order of increasing ratio: 11 (6/11),7 (4/7),17 (10/17),10 (3/5),23 (14/23),13 (8/13),29 (18/29),16 (5/8),19 (12/19),41 (26/41), then sums ≡1 mod3 (1,t,2t) etc., finally 9 (2/3). For each c, find smallest s|n → ratio r; g(c)=r (small c) or 5r for c=4M. Sum g’s → rational p/q; compute (p+q) mod 99991. Pitfalls: ensure s coprime to 3 ⇒ M≡1; for s with 3‑factor use CRT; include all primitive sums up to needed bound.

Insights: f(n)=min c where n=c+a+b, a,b|c, a≠b. Write a=c/p,b=c/q ⇒ n=c(1+1/p+1/q) ⇒ c=n·pq/(pq+p+q). Need D′= (pq+p+q)/gcd(pq,pq+p+q) | n. For M=3^K, smallest p,q giving integer c: (3,6) ⇒c=2/3 M. For 5M, (2,6) ⇒c=3M. For M+small offsets (≡2 mod 3) the minimal D′=5 (p,q)=(2,6) ⇒c=3/5 n. Hence g(0)=2/3, g(4M)=3, each small offset g=3/5. Sum=2/3+3+4·3/5=91/15 ⇒p+q=106 ⇒mod 99991=106. Pitfalls: ensure D′|n, not just D; check divisibility (5 divides all offsets).

Insights: f(n)=min X with X+X/r+X/s=n (r≠s≥2). ⇒X=n·rs/(rs+r+s), L=D/gcd(D,r) must divide n (if 3∤L: c≡−1 mod L; if 3|L: c≡0).  
For n=M+c (M=3^N): M≡1 (mod L) unless 3|L.  
Compute best (r,s) by descending S=1+1/r+1/s.  
c=0 →(3,6), X/M=2/3 →g=2/3.  
c=4M →n=5M, L must divide 5·3^N →(3,6) works →X/M=10/3 →g=10/3.  
c=1848374 →L=25 (c+1≡0) →(2,16), X/M=16/25 →g=⌊2025!·16/25⌋/2025!.  
c=10162574 →L=47 →(2,15), X/M=30/47.  
c=265710644 →L=97 →(2,64), X/M=64/97.  
c=44636594 →L=167 →(2,55), X/M=110/167.  
Sum S=∑⌊2025!·ratio⌋; p=S/gcd(S,2025!), q=2025!/gcd; answer (p+q) mod 99991. Pitfall: ensure L|n condition (c+1 for 3∤L).

Insights: f(N) = min LCM(d₁,d₂,d₃) with d₁+d₂+d₃=N. Optimal triples are (L, L/x, L/y) ⇒ N=S·t, S=D/gcd(x,y), L=xy/gcd(x,y), ratio = xy/D. Need S|N.  

For N=M=3^{2025!}: only S=3^a work ⇒ smallest ratio 2/3 (x=3,y=6) ⇒ f(M)=2M/3, g(0)=2/3.  

For N=5M: S=9 still divides N ⇒ same ratio ⇒ g(4M)=5·2/3=10/3.  

For N=M+c (c≡2 mod 3): S must divide c+1 and be coprime to 3. Compute divisors of c+1, find smallest ratio via pairs (2,16),(2,15),(2,64),(2,55) giving ratios 16/25,30/47,64/97,110/167.  

Sum = 2/3+10/3+16/25+30/47+64/97+110/167 = 125561848/19033825.  

p+q mod 99991 = 8687.  

Pitfalls: use S=D/gcd(x,y) (not D/gcd(xy,D)); handle 3‑powers separately; ensure 2025! divisible by denominators.

Insights: f(n) uses three divisors {1,N/k,N/l} → N=n·kl/(k+l+kl). Require k,l|N ⇒ g=gcd(kℓ,k+l+ℓ) must divide both k,ℓ. Valid (k,l) give L=(k+ℓ+kl)/g, Nnum=kl/g, ratio r=Nnum/L. Minimal r for each n is smallest r with L|n. Compute M=3^E (E huge). For L not divisible by 3, M≡1 (mod L); for L=3^a·m, M≡0 (mod 3^a) and ≡1 (mod m). Check divisibility of n=M+c (c=0,4M,1848374,10162574,265710644,44636594). Valid L’s (sorted by r): 11→6/11,7→4/7,17→10/17,25→16/25,47→30/47,97→64/97,167→110/167,… Only L dividing each n: M→L=27 (r=20/27);5M→L=27 (r=5·20/27=100/27); M+1848374→L=25 (r=16/25); M+10162574→L=47 (r=30/47); M+265710644→L=97 (r=64/97); M+44636594→L=167 (r=110/167). Sum = 20/27+100/27+16/25+30/47+64/97+110/167 = 1206191932/171304425 → p+q≡20341 (mod 99991). Pitfall: exclude (k,l) where gcd(kℓ,k+ℓ+ℓ)∤k or ℓ (e.g., (2,6) invalid).

Insights: f(n)=min c with a,b|c, a≠b, a+b=n−c ⇒ c=n·pq/(pq+p+q). Need D′= (pq+p+q)/gcd(pq,pq+p+q) | n. For M=3^K, smallest divisor>2 of M−1 is 2 ⇒ f(M)=(2/3)M. For 5M, D′=5 works via (p,q)=(2,6) ⇒ f(5M)=3M. For M+small offsets (≡4 mod 5), D′=5 works via (2,6) ⇒ f=n·3/5. Hence g(0)=2/3, g(4M)=3, each small offset g=3/5. Sum=2/3+3+4·3/5=91/15 ⇒ p+q=106. Pitfall: ensure D′|n, not just any p,q.

Insights: M=3^k (k huge). For n=M+c, minimal N often comes from triple (N,N/p,N/q) with sum n ⇒ N=pq·n/(pq+p+q). Need D=pq+p+q|n. Since M≡1 (mod D) when 3∤D, condition reduces to D|(c+1). Find smallest factor pq/D<2/3 ⇒ N<(2/3)M ⇒ f(M+c)<(2/3)M. For c=0, f=(2/3)M; for c=4M, no D works, f> (2/3)M. For c=1848374,10162574,265710644,44636594, D|(c+1) with (p,q)=(2,17),(2,15),(2,65),(2,55) giving factors 34/53,30/47,130/197,110/167 < 2/3, so f<(2/3)M. Thus k=4. Sum = 4−k/2025! = 4−4/2025! ⇒ p+q=5·2025!−4. Compute 2025! mod 99991 → result 86209. (Pitfall: ensure D|n, use M≡1 mod D for 3∤D.)

Insights: f(N)=min LCM(d₁,d₂,d₃) with d₁+d₂+d₃=N. Optimal triples are (L, L/x, L/y) ⇒ N=S·t, S=D/gcd(x,y), ratio = xy/D. For N=M (3^k) only S=3^a work → best (x,y)=(3,6), ratio = 2/3 ⇒ g(0)=2/3. For N=5M, S=9 still works → g(4M)=5·2/3=10/3. For N=M+c (c≠0, c≡2 mod 3) S must divide c+1 and be coprime to 3. Scan pairs (x,y) (≤500) → minimal ratios: c=1848374 →16/25, c=10162574 →30/47, c=265710644 →64/97, c=44636594 →110/167. Sum =125561848/19033825 ⇒ (p+q) mod 99991 = 8687. Insights: f(n)=min c with a,b|c, a≠b, a+b=n−c ⇒ c=n·pq/(pq+p+q). For M=3^K, (pq+p+q) must divide n. For c=0, D=27 ⇒ f(M)=(2/3)M. For n=5M, D=11 works ⇒ f(5M)=(10/3)M. For each small offset c, D=c+1 (since D coprime to 3) ⇒ choose p=2,q such that D=2q+2+q=3q+2 ⇒ q=(D−2)/3 integer. This gives factor pq/D<2/3, so f(M+c)<(2/3)M. Hence g(0)=2/3, g(4M)=10/3, each small offset g= (pq/D)·(1+ c/M)≈pq/D. Sum = 2/3+10/3+4·(pq/D). Compute exact fractions → p+q≡106 (mod 99991). (Pitfall: ensure D|(M+c), not just any p,q.)
